messages:
Omar (AE): Heads-up — Pegasus onramp call tomorrow 10am PT. They want a simple answer: how many reserved GPUs to commit for their initial P0 traffic, what preheat window to ask for, and a short note for their security questionnaire about KMS/HSM usage.
Elaine (SRE): Quick numbers would help. Do we have their expected qps and average tokens per request?
Omar (AE): Sales shared a profile: 600 qps at peak, avg 120 tokens/request, 95% chat latency SLO 250ms p95. Traffic is bursty (30% bursts during daytime).
Sasha (ML Eng): For 120 tokens/request and 600 qps that's ~72k tokens/s -> sustained. With A100-ish throughput and our runtime, rough rule: 1 reserved GPU ~= 150 qps at these lengths with quantized model. So baseline 4 reserved GPUs to meet 600 qps steady.
Matt (Solutions): +1 on math. Add headroom for autoscale failover + KV warmup. Recommend 5 reserved for runway, with autoscale to 8 for bursts. Preheat window 12–30 min depending on cache approach.
Keith (Prod Eng): Important: if they want <250ms p95, we should keep higher reserved baseline or use lower-latency model variant. Autoscale cold starts to quantized variants can add 200–400ms.
Omar (AE): Pricing question from Pegasus: what's the delta MRR if they commit 5 reserved vs 4 reserved? Need a single-line answer for procurement.
Matt (Solutions): Roughly, 1 reserved GPU = $Xk/mo (use pricing sheet). Delta per GPU = $Xk. So 4 -> 5 is +$Xk/mo. (I'll DM exact number from pricing).
Elaine (SRE): Security Q: KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated. For hosted, we provide envelope encryption + optional customer key integration for enterprise (bring-your-key). Document reference: https://redwood.example.com/kms.
Omar (AE): Pegasus asked whether preheat and KV warmup requires additional networking/config from their end (VPC peering etc).
Keith (Prod Eng): For Dedicated we can prewarm without customer changes. For Private/VPC we might need initial peering and a short maintenance window to run KV warmup (12–30 min). Will need a small burst of network egress for model cache pulls.
Sasha (ML Eng): Operational note: KV warmup plan — we'll warm top-n prefixes using historical prompt samples. If they can provide a signature set (5–10k recent prompts) we can get 80–90% hit rate after preheat. Otherwise allow +20% reserved headroom.
Omar (AE): Can someone draft a 2-line note for procurement: "recommended commit / burst plan" + "security answer"? They want to paste into their vendor evaluation form.
Matt (Solutions): Draft below, feel free to paste: "Recommended reserved baseline: 5 GPUs to meet 600 qps steady-state with 120 tokens/request and 250ms p95 target; autoscale policy to allow bursts up to 8 GPUs for traffic spikes. Preheat/kv warmup recommended 12–30 minutes; providing 5–10k representative prompts significantly reduces cold token latency. Pricing delta per GPU: +$Xk/mo — Matt will confirm exact figure"
Elaine (SRE): Security blurb: "Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private and envelope encryption for hosted; HSM-backed key storage is available via enterprise contract; audit logs and key rotation policies provided."
Omar (AE): Perfect. I'll send these to Pegasus. One more: if they want a lower-cost option, can we propose quantized model profile with slightly higher latency but 30% cost savings?
Sasha (ML Eng): Yes — quantized variant trades some latency/quality; expect ~20–30% cost reduction, p95 increases ~50–120ms depending on sequence length. Good for non-interactive batch scenarios.
Omar (AE): Sasha, please add a one-liner about quality tradeoffs I can give them.
Sasha (ML Eng): "Quantized model variant: ~25% lower per-token cost, minor quality delta (depends on eval set); recommended for high-throughput non-latency-sensitive inference."
Omar (AE): Thanks all. Last ask: can infra-bot run a quick simulation for 600 qps/120 tokens with 5 reserved + autoscale to 8 and post expected p95 numbers?
infra-bot: Running simulation... will post results in ~15m. (job 87321)
Matt (Solutions): I'll grab exact pricing and post here in the next message.
Elaine (SRE): Also looping in Legal for a short KMS note in the questionnaire.
Omar (AE): Great — keep this thread for any follow-ups. I'll report back after the call tomorrow. :thumbsup:
